newsitem.title: USA: Sony close to signing deal with Calley.
newsitem.headline: Sony close to signing deal with Calley.

text.p: Sony Corp is close to reaching an agreement with United Artists President John Calley to take a top job at Sony Pictures Entertainment, according to people familar with the negotiations.
Calley, who has been in talks with Sony for several weeks about the studio job would replace Alan Levine, who resigned last week.
According to people familar with the talks, an announcement about Calley and other executive appointments could be made on Tuesday.

It is expected that Calley will be responsible for Sony's motion picture operations and work with current Sony Corp of America Executive Vice President Jeff Sagansky along the lines of how Time Warner Inc's co-Chairmen Bob Daly and Terry Semel operate.
Calley, 65, is credited with revitalizing MGM's ailing United Artists studio with such hits as "Goldeneye", "Leaving Las Vegas" and "Birdcage".
